newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Namibia mulls World Bank loan for Walvis Bay plan.
newsitem.headline: Namibia mulls World Bank loan for Walvis Bay plan.

text.p: Namibia is mulling a World Bank development loan to help construct an export processing zone (EPZ) at the port of Walvis Bay, the bank said on Tuesday.
Pamela Cox, World Bank country director for Namibia, South Africa, Botswana, Lesotho and Swaziland, said the loan was still at the pre-appraisal stage.
"The pre-appraisal mission for that should be going (to Namibia) in a couple of weeks," she told a news conference in Johannesburg.
Cox said the size of any possible loan had not yet been finalised, but that it was likely to fall somewhere around the $35-40 million mark.
"Government is still thinking about it," she said.
The Walvis Bay EPZ initiative was put in place in 1995 to attract overseas investors to the area and boost the competitiveness of local manufacturers with the aim of upping exports of finished goods.
Incentives include providing exporters with a range of incentives such as exemptions from corporate tax, import duties, training grants and preferential access to major foreign markets.
The loan will be used to help fund infrastructure projects around Walvis Bay, the main port of this vast but sparsely populated south-west African country.
